$comment: Single source of truth for site-wide propagation. Hand-edited; consumed by scripts/propagate.mjs. Bumping any value here propagates to every target file the propagator knows about.

counts.$comment: tests convention CHANGED 2026-07-08 (Day 140): now the REGISTERED total (node test runner 'tests' line) to match the SDK's own published number (README badge, package.json), not the passing count. As of 2026-07-08 the suite reports tests 4026, pass 4023, 3 skipped; canonical = 4026. Prior rule used the passing count (was 3959 = pass, with tests 3962); superseded so the site does not contradict the SDK's npm page. modules_total = modules_core + modules_v2. Canonical: modules_v2 = publicly exported logical units via a barrel (src/v2/index.ts or src/index.ts), ratified 2026-05-17 = 23. modules_total = modules_core + modules_v2, DERIVED from the canonical count, never used to justify it. Raw file count, subsystem directory count, and historical project-state values are implementation signals, NOT canonical module counts.

third_party_citations.title: PDR in Production
third_party_citations.note: Independent citation of our work. NOT authored by us. Excluded from counts.papers by definition. It appears in aps-web/llms-full.txt on purpose; any check that counts DOIs in a file against counts.papers will flag that file and the check, not the file, is wrong.

$papers_rule: counts.papers = len(papers). Membership is this list and nothing else. A DOI appearing on a surface is NOT evidence of authorship: third_party_citations are ours to cite and not ours to count. Adding a paper means adding it HERE first, then propagating the LIST to every surface, not just the number.

language_replacements.$comment: Future: copy normalization. Not yet wired in propagate.mjs; documented here as the canonical edit list for any human/CC sweeping prose.
